label: mid-copy step reading 0/1/z/x while outputting a favored token (z,0,x,o,n,1,e,f,c)
explanation: Sparse (~0.26% of steps). Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original phase or on the delimiter), and mostly at recall_idx 3-5 (peaks at 4). It does not fire at recall_idx 0-1 or once 6 or more outputs remain, and is rare at recall_idx 2. It is strongly token-selective: the input token is usually 0 (about 50% of mass, highest activations), then 1, z, x, and less often e, c, f. It is also more likely when the token being output is in {z,0,x,o,n,1,e,f,c}, when the previous input is from a similar set, and in sequences with more digits or repeated tokens. Activations seem to add up across these token preferences (input, previous input, output) rather than follow one clean rule, so precision stays low: most mid-copy steps reading 0 are inactive. The predicate covers about 80% of activation mass at about 18% precision.
